World's First Aero-Electric Travel Trailer Is a Futuristic Home for 4 That Expands at Camp
26 photos
Photo: Lightship
Some three years ago, U.S.-based startup Lightship broke on the RV scene with a concept for a travel trailer – of the future! – that went viral almost immediately. Initially called the Lightship L1, that futuristic RV has grown into the Lightship AE.1 and now, as a 2027 model year, is shipping to first customers nationwide.
Lightship AE.1 is dubbed the world's first aero-electric travel trailer, but as neat as that might sound, it's not even the most impressive thing about it. That would be the sum of all its features: its self-sufficiency, its low profile in travel mode and yet the ability to offer true creature comforts, its sustainability, and its ultra-smart characteristics.
This travel trailer is unlike any other on the market right now, and that's not just a way of saying. It was designed to be different, built to be different, and the result is – obviously – different.
The AE.1 debuted in prototype form at the 2025 CES in Las Vegas, almost two years after its introduction as a concept at SXSW. At the time, limited production for the founders' edition, which Lightship called the AE.1 Cosmos Edition, was scheduled to kick off by the summer of that year, with deliveries for those 50 first units to follow.
Photo: Lightship Lightship is now saying that production is on track, so that probably means that plans announced for the other three trims, Atmos, Panos, and Terros, will probably proceed as scheduled as well. Before that happens, though, Lightship is offering a better look at the 2027 AE.1 through the video tour below, taking place at their California facility.
Here's Many of Beer Run Bus touring the 2027 version of the viral travel trailer and then getting a tour of the facility. It's the perfect chance to see what modifications Lightship has implemented as well as to see how the production version of the 2025 prototype is shaping up. This video tour also offers a bunch of new specs that weren't made public with the debut of that prototype.
Designed & built different As already noted, the Lightship AE.1 is different in every aspect you can think of. Built on a steel chassis with aluminum frame and fiberglass body, it comes with an interior packed with sustainable and extra-durable materials, from the woven vinyl flooring to the composite underfloor and composite counters.
Photo: Lightship Cabinetry is all aluminum, with lattice-style doors and full aluminum construction, both for the drawers and cabinets. The upholstery is recycled plastic and wool, so it's durable, dirt-resistant, and nice to the touch, offering a homey vibe to offset the rather austere, almost sterile interior walls.
The layout is different from a traditional travel trailer , too, because Lightship opts to have a canopy roof that lifts and lowers on actuators for an easier towing experience. That means that you can't have actual rooms inside, and the only door and wall you'll find onboard are to the rear, full-width bathroom.
Dimensions haven't changed. The AE.1 is a 26.7 feet (8.1 meters) long, 8.5 feet (2.5 meters) wide, and 7 feet (2.1 meters) high in travel mode, expanding to 10 feet (3 meters) in total height at camp to offer 7.5 feet (2.2 meters) of interior headroom.
Photo: Lightship Gross weight is 8,300 lbs (3,765 kg) but the AE.1 is meant to offer a comparable easier towing experience thanks to the TrekDrive system on the tandem axle, consisting of a 400V motor moving the wheels in conjunction with the array of sensors in the vicinity of the towbar. Lightship AE.1 is meant to reduce the impact on the range of the towing vehicle, whether it's an electric or a gas-fueled one.
Another way in which towing impact is reduced is through enhanced aerodynamics , which is where the collapsible canopy comes in. It's not just an aesthetic choice or a weird flex, helping reduce drag by effectively scaling down the footprint of the trailer behind the towing vehicle.
Control of the canopy is either manual, with a physical button available on the box at the front, or fully automated, through the companion Atlas app you can use on the provided tablet/touchscreen panel or your phone. For extra safety, Lightship includes a thorough checklist of stuff you should be mindful of before closing down the canopy.
Photo: Lightship Large, frameless and slightly tinted windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens offer 270-degree panoramic views inside. The interior remains usable even with the canopy down, though you won't be enjoying the views in that case. You won't have full functionality inside, but you can still sit down for a quick meal, get some work done, have a nap, or use the bathroom.
Self-sufficiency & comfort The Lightship AE.1 comes with as much as 77kWh of lithium batteries built into the steel underbody chassis and a roof lined with 1,800W of solar panels. That's more than enough to run house functions without restrictions, to charge the towing vehicle, or even use the massive battery bank as backup for the home in case of an emergency.
Photo: Lightship Also on the topic of autonomy, the AE.1 carries 50 gallons (189 liters) of freshwater, 25 gallons (95 liters) of gray, and 30 gallons (113.5 liters) of black water.
Inside, you have a Switchback Lounge at the front, which is a lounge arrangement with two levels and a mattress that flips out into a queen bed. That's one of the two available sleeping spaces, not including the optional Summit Sleeper, which is a double drop down bed that's not included in the demo unit.
The other sleeping space is the dinette, which converts by dropping the table at the press of another button. During the day, it's spacious and comfortable to sit up to six people, but it will only accommodate two of them at night.
Photo: Lightship The kitchen starts to left side of the extra-wide entry way, so you have plenty of worktop space and a decent amount of storage options. A large, stainless steel sink is available as you advance to the rear of the trailer, across from the main kitchen block, which is equipped with a two-burner induction cooktop, a water-efficient dishwasher, a convection microwave oven, and a marine-grade fridge with freezer.
Again, storage is limited to the lower part of the trailer, but Lightship compensates for that with the modular CargoCraft modular storage system consisting of open cubbies you attach on rail tracks over the windows – and subsequently remove when you pack up camp to head back home.
The full-width bathroom is hidden behind opaque plastic walls and comes with a plumbed porcelain toilet, a small sink with storage below and overhead, and a flush-floor shower with a curtain. Being built out of the same easy-to-dry and easy-to-clean composites, not having a step-up or step-in shower allows it to be extra spacious and comfortable.
Photo: Lightship The Lightship AE.1 also comes with electric auto-leveling, four corner stabilizers, a backup camera, three exterior color choices, a large pass-through storage compartment at the front, a Seaflo water pump, and a 20,000-BTU AC unit with a heat pump inside the front box that services the entire trailer.
Prices start at around $157,000 for the most basic version and go as high as $250,000 for the Cosmos variant shown below.

The dumb oil war in Iran is driving up the cost of just about everything , including new cars. That’s giving Chinese EVs a huge advantage over Western “legacy” car brands already lagging in tech and struggling with affordability – and those legacy brands about to have a whole new to them problem on their hands: USED Chinese EVs .
Western automakers have leaned on protectionist trade policies to keep cheaper Chinese rivals at bay, placing strict limits on the number of new Chinese cars allowed in and hefty tariffs on new battery-electric vehicles (BEVs) are as high as 45.3% in the EU. That supply limitation is, of course, ratcheting up demand for the high-tech, low-cost Chinese machines, and buyers in Europe and Canada are finding that used Chinese EVs – which offer comparable tech to the newest Western EVs, a price tag up to 40% lower than their already low MSRPs, and which are not subject to the same protectionist import duties – are a workable alternative.
According to data shared by importers/exporters China EV Marketplace ( CEVM ), pre-owned vehicle sales to EU customers grew 280% year over year, with sales climbing to 7,900 units through September.
“Tariffs have already weakened demand for new Chinese BEVs among our European customers. We expect the hybrid import cap to put pressure on new PHEV sales too,” CEVM COO Jakub Geršl told CarNewsChina . “Pre-owned cars are exempt from the additional BEV tariffs and from the new hybrid (PHEV) quota. That is why we are making pre-owned vehicles the main focus of our European business.”
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Relentless progress
A shipment of Lotus Cars arrives in Canada; via Geely.
CEVM has more than 2,600 used Chinese EVs on its website as I type this, and their inventory is refreshed almost daily with fresh pre-owned examples of cars from brands like BYD, Geely, Zeekr, and others – and the company claims its prices are about 40% below the original price (MSRP) on average.
“Lower new-car prices put pressure on pre-owned prices as well,” Geršl adds. “Our Shanghai-based team searches for those opportunities. We regularly find cars with around 6,000 km on the clock priced 40% below their original Chinese list price.”
That price reduction is driven by a number of factors, including the relentless march of technological progress, the flood of new and updated EVs coming out of Chinese car brands, and a burgeoning domestic Chinese car culture that values newness above all else. If you’re reading between the lines there, I think you’ll find that that means more low-mileage, low-price, high-tech, and high-value Chinese EVs are coming to the West – and probably a lot sooner than brands like VW, who are struggling to compete as it is , would want.
And that’s the real problem – whether you agree with him or not, Elon Musk will tell you that technology and markets move faster than legislation , and once consumers go electric, precious few of them ever go back to gas or diesel , regardless of what that dude filming himself wearing PitVipers in the drivers’ seat of his pickup and your racist uncle on Facebook are telling you.
Top comment by Philip234
Liked by 8 people
All kidding aside, this is fundamentally upending all of the transportation forecast around the world. The flood of used Chinese EVs hitting emerging markets is poised to massively accelerate electrification of transport far faster than anyone anticipated. The industry is so obsessed with the new car market (only 30% of the car market) that it missed the impact of China exporting recent model used vehicles across the emerging world at extremely attractive prices. This allows for faster refresh inside China without out-of-control ballooning of the vehicle fleet. The world is going to wake up in 2035 and realize emerging markets in Africa and Central Asia significantly electrified without big EV sales while no one noticed.

8-Second 1/4-Mile King for Sale: This Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 Is Brand New
9 photos
Photo: VanguardMotorSales
Muscle cars still do not get more exciting than the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 , even if this model hasn’t been around for a few years now.
Ford hasn’t been able to top it with a crazy version of its S650 Mustang, and if you said GTD, then you should know that it is less powerful. Like a lot less powerful. It has 753 horsepower at the wheels and 815 horsepower at the crank, according to the spec sheet, and it costs $320,000+. And that may be superior to the new Mustang Dark Horse SC, it is nowhere as exciting as the Demon 170.
Meanwhile, the folks at Chevrolet do not have a muscle car in their lineup anymore. The Camaro has been dead for almost three years now, but recently rumors claim that the moniker is returning, not on a two-door model, but on a four-door, as the future of the Camaro is reportedly a sedan. However, if the information turns out to be correct, then it will offer V8 power, and perhaps a stick shift option.
Dodge’s modern-day muscle car, meanwhile, is still unavailable with a V8 engine, but that will reportedly change starting in late 2027, as the 2028 model year Charger is expected to go down the V8-powered route in a premiere. And knowing how Dodge tends to roll, we wouldn’t be surprised to learn that the Demon 170’s successor is a few years away, and we really hope that it is, because this model deserves a modern continuation.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales Now, despite not being in production anymore, there are still quite a few units of the Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 that have only a few miles under their belts. Some of them hit the used car market occasionally, and the example pictured in the gallery above is one of them. According to the vendor, Vanguard Motor Sales, this machine has only 245 miles (394 km) on the clock. Thus, you are looking at a brand new muscle car, albeit one that was launched for the 2023 model year.
This machine features a blue paint finish on the outside, sprinkled with some yellow on the OEM apron, and some black on various components. The wheels are shod in drag radials, from what we can see, and the interior offers a mix of black leather and Alcantara upholstery, with some white stitching for a bit of contrast. And despite the fact that we are looking at a new ride, there is some wear on the driver’s seat outer bolster.
The 2023 Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 in question has an ultra-clean underbody, and the engine bay is also squeaky clean. This is where the 6.2-liter supercharged V8 mill rests, and it is a heavily upgraded version of the famous Hellcat lump that can run on E10, making 900 hp (913 ps/627 kW) and 810 lb-ft (1,097 Nm) of torque.
Fill the tank with E85, though, and those numbers will increase to 1,025 horsepower (1,039 ps/764 kW) and 945 pound-feet (1,280 Nm) of torque. As you likely remember, this model needs a neck-snapping 1.66 seconds to sprint to 60 mph (97 kph), albeit in perfect conditions, with a skilled driver holding the wheel, and a bit of luck. On a good day, it will run the standing 1/4-mile in 8.91 seconds at 151.17 mph (243.28 kph), though we’ve seen some that have turned out to be even quicker, and that’s with no tuning job involved.
Photo: VanguardMotorSales Dodge’s Challenger SRT Demon 170 remains a great machine that has been born for drag racing, and it feels right at home at the drag strip. And despite being dead and buried, it is still on the very pricey side of things, because this model usually fetches from $125,000 to $145,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America.
Some of them tend to be even more expensive, especially the brand-new examples, and the model had an initial MSRP of $96,666, in case you forgot. However, the insane dealer markups made it pretty much impossible to land one at a decent price, and the initial resale value brought this model very close to the $250K mark. Needless to say that the market has cooled significantly since then, as we told you in the above paragraph.
Now, this Dodge Challenger SRT Demon 170 is brand new, has a mere 245 miles under its belt, and other than some wear on the driver’s seat, it is as new as they get. So, how much do you think you will have to fork out if you dream about parking it in your garage and driving it whenever you want to? Well, signing your name on the dotted line means transferring $179,900 to the selling dealer, as this was the asking price at the time of writing.
But is it worth $180K? You be the judge of that, and if you want to see more of this muscle car, then you can do so here on the quoted website.

The Camplife Apres 170 Is What Camper Van Luxury Looks Like When Budget Is the Only Limit
20 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs
Camper van luxury can take many forms. For me, the utmost luxury is to be able to enjoy proper home-like comforts in a vehicle that lets you explore far and wide - that's exactly the type of project I'd like to share with you.
Today's featured build is based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It's the work of Camplife Customs, a San Diego, California-based company that provides custom van and camper van conversions – it specializes in bringing your dreams to life, with budget being the only limitation.
Camplife Customs offers multiple types of conversions. This one is a top-of-the-line conversion called the Apres 170, a luxurious and reliable mobile retreat based on the Sprinter 170.
As always, let's first take a look at the van's exterior. You can tell that this vehicle is meant for adventuring as soon as you lay eyes on it. To make good use of the AWD capabilities, Camplife Customs installed Black Rhino Armory wheels wrapped in 33-inch Cooper Discoverer all-terrain tires.
The company further improved on the stock off-roading capabilities by fitting a Van Compass suspension kit, which offers a 3-inch (7-centimeter) lift and front and rear shocks.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs At the rear, you'll come across a Vanspeed spare tire carrier / ladder combo that allows for quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll find a powder-coated rack holding a front-facing LED light bar, a Fiamma F45S awning, and two 200 W solar panels.
Other notable mods are Vanspeed side steps and power and water connections. I saved the best for last - the most significant exterior mod is a hardsided rooftop tent. It has windows on all sides (one of which is an awning-style window), a 3-inch-thick mattress that can accommodate two adults, and ceiling lights.
Enter, and you'll be greeted by a high-end, beautifully designed interior. You'll notice bamboo cabinetry, a hexagonal tiled ceiling with recessed LED light strips, and dark plank flooring. The look is complemented by a white solid surface countertop and a brass trim – it's actually brass and not just a material that imitates it.
The interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space. What's more, the passenger seat is mounted on a swivel base, so it can be turned around to face the back of the van. The driver's seat cannot be swiveled because a tall closet is positioned right behind it.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs Straight ahead as you step inside, Camplife Customs devised the bathroom. It boasts a shower, a Laveo dry-flush toilet hidden on a heavy-duty slide with its own compartment, and walls covered with a Flexlite material that has a marble finish with a gold inlay.
The shower has a cool fixture with three heads: a sprayer for feet, an overhead one, and a bigger handheld wand. Moreover, a Nautilus retractable door prevents water from splashing outside the bathroom.
Next, we have the kitchen on the passenger side. It features a deep stainless steel sink with a rotating faucet, a two-burner stovetop, and a flip-up table. With the use of the latter, you get about 74 inches (188 centimeters) of usable counter space.
Two overhead cabinets, seven drawers, and a cabinet underneath the sink are available for storage. On the front end of the overhead units, you'll find a battery monitor, an inverter switch, lighting controls, and a controller for the rooftop tent.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs The rest of the kitchen amenities are on the opposite side – you'll notice a floor-to-ceiling unit integrating a pull-out pantry, three drawers (one of which is hidden), a closet, and a 90-liter Norcold fridge with a tiny freezer compartment. Furthermore, above, you'll discover the pass-through that leads into the rooftop tent.
In the back of the living space, Camplife Customs created a dinette area that sits on a raised platform. It comprises three benches that form a "U" shape, with a large table in the middle. If you drop down the table and rearrange the cushions, you can turn this space into a sleeping arrangement.
The reason why the dinette area sits higher is to make a bit of room for a garage underneath it. This setup is also why there are no overhead cabinets – you would've hit your head on them.
The garage underneath the bed is accessible only from the back of the van after opening the two rear doors. Besides offering a decent amount of storage space, the garage houses the utility systems. A compartment deeper inside it accommodates a Velit 12V A/C unit.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs Power is on the right side – the electrical system's highlights are an 800 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter. Two charging sources are available: shore power and solar power.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 22-gallon (83-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank of the same capacity, a Fogatti water heater, and an outdoor shower.
The same plumbing box holds a propane canister. The last important system that will make a huge difference in colder environments is a floor heating system powered with electricity.
All in all, Camplife Customs made sure to pack this capable camper van with tons of luxuries, all efficiently arranged in a tastefully designed space.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Camplife Customs As initially mentioned, this rig, which has just 5,000 miles (8,047 km), is now for sale – unfortunately, we don't know any pricing information regarding this specific build. We do know that a full van conversion by Camplife Customs can range from $75,000 to $200,000 (€66,698 to €177,862), excluding the base vehicle price.

2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV: How Does the Dedicated Performance Crossover SUV Fare Against Its Rivals?
63 photos
Photo: Mercedes-AMG
Believe it or not, the 2027 Mercedes-AMG GT SUV, which has a dedicated EV architecture and no correspondent in the Mercedes-Benz family, isn’t coming as a completely unique proposition on the automotive market sometime next year. Instead, it has foes – and some of them are already on sale!
The automotive world has gone to different extremes lately: some automakers have finally understood that people need affordable models, and Stellantis, for example, came up with the Citroen 2CV concept at the 2026 Paris Motor Show, while others only seem to think that the one-percenters matter. The latter roster is beginning to look quirkier by the day, given the existence of the likes of the Xiaomi SU7 Ultra, Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, or the Ferrari Luce and the newly introduced Jaguar Type 01.
Sure, the Xiaomi SU7 is a full-size four-door sedan EV, just like the others, but it doesn’t cost a fortune like its Western foes. But would it be a fair comparison nowadays if we didn’t include at least one Chinese EV into every discussion? This one is fashioned after the initial batch of high-performance EV sedans, all aimed at taking down the now-defunct Tesla Model S Plaid: Taycan, Lucid Air, and all the other failed attempts from various startups that aren’t even worth mentioning.
Now, the new kids on the block, the Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, Ferrari Luce, plus the Jaguar Type 01, aim for a different thing: they want to mesmerize not only via their high-tech powertrains but also because they can stand out in any crowd, even the wrong ones.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG Unlike the original Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupe, which was essentially a high-performance CLS fastback sedan, the new EV has numerous styling issues according to virtual artists, like the disrespect for the front fascia zones, the pretending fish mouth (also at the front), or the random LED circle positions and the massive switch for the key volume from the bottom to the top around the back.
The Ferrari Luce, meanwhile, emanates zero passion, has ‘Apple radius’ elements everywhere (read ‘round corners’), a static profile, and a ‘swallowed’ rear. The Jaguar, also, has gone from cool to cold and static with a brutalist profile and an industrial AC unit rear… It would be a little better if not for the overly generic style, which made it interchangeable with the Range Rover and even the new Freelander brand by the virtual artists.
Now, after this lengthy intro and thoughts on the EV sedans, here comes the Mercedes-AMG GT SUV , the first of its kind, and the all-electric crossover SUV counterpart of the GT 4-Door, obviously. Naturally, it comes in the same three versions, with up to 1,153 hp on tap. But what do you know, the situation has changed a little, and at first glance we’re dealing with something that’s a little better from the design standpoint.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG That is simply because it looks like the designers first crated the SUV and then worked around it for the sedan, given that all the styling elements now work a little better on the crossover – the larger volume occupied by the SUV allows the very harsh graphics to breathe more than on the GT 4-Door. The SUV now feels a bit more structured at the front and comes with stunning wheels plus a slightly less vulgar rear end.
But that’s just the first step in the right direction. The interior, meanwhile, is take it or leave it, as AMG opted for the same three-screen layout, just organized differently, and on a vertical scale rather than tilted toward the windscreen, even if ever so slightly. Breaking the dashboard into two different layers also doesn’t help much, since the main problem with this approach is the massive bezels, actually. We live in the world of smartphones with invisible bezels, and automakers need to consider that.
Anyway, let’s talk about the competition. Have you seen the new Bentley Torcal? Don’t dismiss it as a different EV animal, because it shares the internals with the Porsche Cayenne Electric and only costs more and has a different style – one that seeks to fight the Ferrari Purosangue and Rolls-Royce Cullinan. But it’s pretty clear that buyers will cross-shop with the AMG GT SUV before settling on one or the other.
Photo: Mercedes-AMG Now for the direct foes, which are the Lucid Gravity from America, the Lotus Eletre from China-UK, and the Porsche Cayenne Electric from Germany . There will be a Neue Klasse BMW iX5 M, for sure, but it’s still brewing, so we can’t talk about that one. The Lucid is a stylish model, one that doesn’t emphasize a heavy design and instead offers massive horsepower options like the Gravity GT-S with 1,070 horsepower. It also has great range and advanced battery technology, and it’s right now available on the market.
The Lotus Eletre R is a pure hyper-SUV focusing on heavy track-inspired dynamics, and if you can live with the Chinese DNA, it will give you 905 hp and a time to 62 mph of less than three seconds. Sure, it’s the least powerful of the bunch, as even the Porsche Cayenne Turbo Electric can do more: 1,140 hp, and it charges at close to 400 kW to make it faster than the other two at DC ultra-fast charging stations. On the other hand, the AMG GT SUV tops them all with up to 710 kW DC max charging, setting a new industry standard…

1965 Ford Mustang Fastback Is a Shelby GT 350R Tribute With 'Extra Seasoning.' It Won't Sell Cheap
10 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
Sitting proudly in the inventory of Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors , this spectacular 1965 Mustang Fastback Shelby GT 350R tribute looks readily dressed to impress. But it won’t come home with you unless you’re bankable…
Ford's longest nameplate in continuous production, the Mustang , sold ‘just’ 9,960 units across the US automotive market during the third quarter of the year, with 38,685 examples of the breed sold yar-to-date, up almost 18% compared to last year. That’s a far cry for the S650 iteration, the seventh by its name, compared to the 1965 Mustang, which sold over 400k units in its first year of availability!
But hey, times were different back then, and it’s really no surprise that a lot of people continue to praise the ’65 Mustang over anything else. But how about a modified one? Well, here’s “a classic example of the first-generation Mustang transformed into a purpose-built performance machine,” with this 1965 Ford Mustang Fastback rocking a frame-off custom build, according to the dealer, as well as “a striking blue and orange livery inspired by the competition Mustangs of the era.”
The classic livery even features “some new old stock decals,” and the car also comes with the period-correct "extractor" rear window with integrated center brake light or an in-trunk fuel cell with "gas hole." All in all, the description says it’s a “pure old school race car with just enough street car sprinkled on and the power and control to take the GT350R experience to Spinal Tap levels at a quality level worthy of the cover of the January 2025 issue of Hemmings Muscle Machines.”
That’s specific, right? Anyway, here are the details. The fastback comes with a “302-based oversquare 363ci Small Block Ford V8 featuring quad Weber 48s and forged internals, pumping out north of 500 horsepower,” a five-speed Tremec TKX with overdrive for “comfortable street driving,” a custom chassis, a street or track coilover suspension, and disc brakes with a three-link rear conversion fitted with a 3.89 9-inch rear end featuring a Detroit Locker plus a front rack and pinion conversion.
The alloys are 17-inch Minilite-style rims, and now there’s also a side exhaust breathing through a set of long tubes and Spintech mufflers “for the right sound,” while the Gulf Oil livery is contrasted by the black interior featuring a “four-point roll bar, Cypher adjustable buckets, four-point harnesses, and carbon Autometer Ultra-Lite gauges.”
Naturally, this crazy build (created by MotorCity Grind of Detroit, Michigan) isn’t selling cheap. After all, it was featured in the #257 January 2025 Issue Hemmings Muscle Machines magazine as their cover car. Well, the damage to the bank account is quite obvious: the dealership wants no less than $184,900 to part ways with this particular example. Cool or not?
